title: A leaderboard
description:
Sort players in several ways with key functions.

```
By score:
  1. Cy     980  (level 12)
  2. Ada    950  (level 14)
  3. Bob    950  (level 9)
  4. Dee    720  (level 14)
By level, then name:
  Ada 14, Dee 14, Cy 12, Bob 9
Top 2 under level 13: Cy, Bob
```
hints: A key can return a tuple, which sorts by its first item and then the next: `key=lambda p: (-p["score"], p["name"])` (lesson 5.03).
`enumerate(ranked, start=1)` numbers the rows. `f"{p['name']:<6}"` pads a name to 6 characters.
requirements: Sort by score (highest first); equal scores by name A to Z.
Sort by level (highest first), then name.
Do not change the original list; use `sorted` with `key=`.
stretch: Use `operator.itemgetter` for one of the keys, and add a rank that is shared by equal scores (1, 1, 3).
